# ChainBloom

> Grow a shared history with Bitcoin.
>
> ChainBloom is a Bitcoin protocol for shared creative history. People join
> a world, add to a path, and every step is a real Bitcoin transaction that
> anyone can replay from the chain.

ChainBloom has no project token, no custody, and no trading venue. The
Bitcoin Universe capability snapshot records no marketplace for ChainBloom,
so no Bitcoin Universe product implements a buy, sell, or settle path for
anything created with it.

Every link below is a page this site publishes.

## Site

- [ChainBloom](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/): the public introduction,
  with the five actions and the questions worth asking before you take part.
- [ChainBloom documentation](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/): ChainBloom lets a group of people grow one shared story, one confirmed Bitcoin moment at a time. Start where you are.

## Start here

- [Start here](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/start/): Answer one question about what you want to do, and get an ordered reading path you can keep, with your place saved in this browser.
- [ChainBloom in 60 seconds](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/start/chainbloom-in-60-seconds/): A world is a bounded shared story. Each path inside it moves one confirmed Bitcoin step at a time. Nobody can rearrange it afterwards, and nobody owns it.
- [Why ChainBloom exists](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/start/why-chainbloom-exists/): Three ordinary problems ruin shared creative work: a feed with no shape, a group voice that flattens into one, and a record only its host can vouch for. One structure answers all three.
- [Watch a world grow](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/start/watch-a-world-grow/): A three-path world from its first moment to its last, in nine steps you can follow with no wallet, no signing, and nothing spent.

## How it works

- [How it works](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/): Six short pages that take you from "a world is a bounded story" to knowing exactly what a confirmed step means and why nobody can reorder it afterwards.
- [How a world grows](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/how-a-world-grows/): An invitation, a fixed number of paths, steps that each wait for the one before them, and an ending that was set on the first day.
- [Worlds, paths, and history](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/worlds-paths-and-history/): What a world fixes forever the moment it is created, what a path actually is, what counts as history, and the four states a path can be in when you find it.
- [Create, Bloom, Echo, Meet and Close](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/the-five-actions/): Five moves build every ChainBloom world: open it, add a moment, answer an earlier one, share a moment with someone, and end a path on purpose.
- [How two paths meet without losing themselves](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/when-paths-meet/): A meeting lets two people share one moment in one transaction while both paths carry on unchanged: nothing is merged, swapped or handed over.
- [How Bitcoin confirmations create shared ordering](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/bitcoin-and-shared-order/): Bitcoin is in ChainBloom for one job: letting strangers agree on what came first, with no referee and no host to trust.
- [Confirmed and unconfirmed activity](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/learn/confirmed-and-unconfirmed/): How to tell a real moment from a hopeful one, why an unconfirmed step can vanish or change position, and what a broadcast receipt is actually worth.

## Take part

- [Take part](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/): The nine pages you need before, during, and after you sign, from opening a world to completing a path, written for the moment money is involved.
- [Creating a world from start to finish](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/create-a-world/): Every decision that goes into opening a world, in the order you have to make them, including the four settings that can never be changed once the transaction confirms.
- [Joining and contributing to a world](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/join-a-world/): How to get a path, decide what your one moment adds, and sign your first step, plus the two things you must check before the transaction goes out.
- [Returning to an existing path](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/return-to-a-path/): Three things to write down before you close the tab, how to check where your path stands weeks later, and what to do if the world moved on without you.
- [Completing a path](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/complete-a-path/): An ending is a contribution, not an exit: what completing does to a path, what it returns to you, and how it differs from letting a world run out.
- [Wallet connection and transaction review](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/wallet-and-review/): Connecting a wallet shares one address and never your keys. This page shows what to read on a signing screen before you approve a ChainBloom step, and what should make you stop.
- [Network fees and confirmation expectations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/fees-and-confirmation/): There are only two costs, a miner fee and the small amount of bitcoin carried inside each path output that returns to you when the path completes. This page shows how both behave.
- [Protecting a live path](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/protect-your-path/): A live path is one specific small Bitcoin output, and an ordinary payment that spends it ends the path for good. Here is how to make sure that never happens.
- [Bookmarks, profiles, watchlists and notifications](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/follow-and-return/): None of these features exist yet, so here is the four-line note that lets you find your way back to any world or path with no software at all, plus what the tools must do when they arrive.
- [Exploring timelines and relationships](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/participate/explore-timelines/): A world's history is a fixed order of confirmed events, and that order can be drawn as a picture, played as a score, or listed as plain text. All three are faithful readings.

## Example worlds

- [Example worlds](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/): Eight worlds worked out in full: the invitation to send, the settings to type in, the moment the paths meet, and how each one ends.
- [A collaborative digital garden](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/collaborative-garden/): Six neighbours, six beds, one shared record of a growing season that nobody can tidy up or rewrite once it is over.
- [A festival history](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/festival-history/): Five stages keep five separate records across six days, and on the closing night they meet, so the festival ends as one thing instead of five.
- [A musical composition](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/musical-composition/): Four players hold four voices for a month, a meeting is a chord two people sign together, and the piece is finished only when every voice has ended itself.
- [A community time capsule](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/community-time-capsule/): One path for each year of a group's life, filled quietly over twelve months and opened out loud on a single evening that everyone can put in the diary.
- [A classroom constellation](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/classroom-constellation/): One path per student across a term, so a class learns what "confirmed" means by waiting for it instead of being told about it.
- [A museum exhibition](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/museum-exhibition/): Visitors shape a bounded work across the run of a show, and the finished history stays readable long after the walls come down.
- [A city or neighbourhood story](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/neighbourhood-story/): One path per street, meeting where the streets actually meet, with a record that holds no addresses and no names.
- [An artist and audience collaboration](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/examples/artist-and-audience/): The artist keeps one line and hands the other four to the audience, and every answer the artist gives is a signature both people put on the same moment.

## For you

- [For you](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/): Eleven short pages, one for each kind of person who arrives here. Find the one that sounds like you, read it in four minutes, and skip the rest.
- [If you are new here](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/new-visitors/): The ninety second version of ChainBloom, the one thing worth looking at first, and clear permission to stop reading afterwards.
- [If you want to take part](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/participants/): What you need before your first step, what it actually costs, what stays yours afterwards, and the three things that can never be undone.
- [If you want to create a world](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/world-creators/): The four choices that can never be changed once you broadcast, how to write an invitation people actually answer, and how to look after the people who answer it.
- [If you make or curate work](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/artists-and-curators/): A bounded, ordered, openly interpretable record behaves like a material you work with, not a platform you publish on. Holding a path is not a copyright claim.
- [If you run a community](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/communities/): How to build a ritual that repeats, keep many voices instead of flattening them into one, moderate before the invitation goes out, and avoid turning taking part into a score.
- [Museums and cultural organizations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/museums-and-cultural-organizations/): Programme a ChainBloom world as a commission: what to budget for real network fees, how to keep it accessible, what survives the run, and what to put on the wall.
- [Educators](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/educators/): What a class actually learns by running a ChainBloom world (shared state, ordering, irreversibility, and collaboration), plus the real limits on cost, consent, age, and keys.
- [Brands and sponsors](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/brands-and-sponsors/): Sponsorship can fund an artist, a programme, access, and production. It cannot buy the history, a reward scheme, or any claim about value.
- [Developers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/developers/): What the ChainBloom package gives you today, the shape of an integration, and which four files to read first.
- [Wallet and explorer integrators](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/wallet-and-explorer-integrators/): Two behaviours decide whether ChainBloom is safe inside your product: never spend a live path output in an ordinary payment, and never show a preview as if it were confirmed.
- [Indexers and operators](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/audiences/indexers-and-operators/): What it takes to serve the same ChainBloom history as everyone else: a Bitcoin node, deterministic replay, rollback on reorganization, and failing closed on an invalid spend.

## Public programs

- [Public programs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/programs/): The operational half of ChainBloom: how a museum, festival, school or community group runs a world as a real public programme, and what it owes the people who take part.
- [Organizations, exhibitions and public programs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/programs/organizations/): What kinds of public programme suit a ChainBloom world, what the budget actually buys, the promises you must never make, and how to judge success without counting trades.
- [Running a world as an exhibition](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/programs/exhibitions/): The floor-level detail of putting a ChainBloom world in a gallery: the staffed station, the wall text, visitors with no wallet, fees on an institutional budget, and what survives closing night.
- [Education and classroom use](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/programs/education/): How to run a ChainBloom world across a school or university term: what it teaches, consent and age, who holds the keys, what it costs per student, and a version that spends nothing at all.
- [Community moderation and participant privacy](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/programs/moderation-and-privacy/): Nobody can remove a confirmed contribution from Bitcoin, so moderation happens before and around a world rather than after it. A contribution also reveals more than people expect.
- [Accessibility for creative worlds](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/programs/accessibility/): What a ChainBloom experience owes its audience: text for every visual, a still for anything that moves, colour that is never the only signal, keyboard access, and plain words about cost.

## Technical reference

- [Technical reference](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/): Everything ChainBloom enforces, read from the source: marker bytes, transaction shapes, validation codes, state, and reorganization handling.
- [Protocol architecture](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/protocol-architecture/): The design in one page: what ChainBloom fixes for everyone, what it leaves open, and the exact bytes of the marker that names an action.
- [Transaction lifecycle](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/transaction-lifecycle/): Where every input and output must sit in a ChainBloom transaction, operation by operation, with the value and script type each position requires.
- [Data structures](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/data-structures/): Every field of WorldState, LaneState, EventState and the rest, with the exact rule behind each lane status and world status.
- [Validation rules](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/validation-rules/): Every check validateProtocolTransaction runs, grouped and named by the issue code it emits, including the two rules people get wrong most often.
- [Reorganizations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/reorganizations/): How a ChainBloom view stays correct when Bitcoin replaces its newest blocks: contiguous apply, one-block rollback, and replay from a common ancestor.
- [Indexer requirements](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/indexer-requirements/): What a service must do so that anyone replaying the same Bitcoin blocks rebuilds exactly the same ChainBloom history, event for event.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/sdk/): Install the package from the repository, encode markers, build every PSBT, validate a transaction, and replay blocks with the reference state engine.
- [Command line](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/cli/): Every command the chainbloom binary has, with a real invocation, the JSON it prints, and the error shape it uses when something goes wrong.
- [Wallet integration](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/integration-wallets/): The three things a wallet owes a ChainBloom user, in priority order, with the exact rule for recognising a path output and the exact rules for signing one.
- [Explorer and gallery integration](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/integration-explorers/): What a viewer must show for a reader to trust it, what it must never claim, and why a rendering of a world is a reading rather than the record.
- [Test vectors](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/test-vectors/): Eleven fixed byte strings that tell you whether your ChainBloom reader agrees with every other one. Five markers that must parse and six that must be refused.
- [Error and issue codes](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/errors/): Every code ChainBloom can produce, the difference between a thrown error and a recorded issue, and what to do about the five you will meet most.
- [Security model](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/security-model/): What ChainBloom protects, what it cannot protect, and the small number of things that are yours to do. Written so you can decide before you sign anything.
- [Reliability and continuity](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/reliability/): Why a ChainBloom history survives the failure of any website that shows it, what a good service does while it is behind, and how to check a moment yourself.
- [Governance and contributing](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/governance/): How the protocol is looked after, what stewardship is there to protect, how a change gets proposed, and the private path for reporting a security problem.
- [Version, changes and what is next](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/reference/changelog/): The current version stated plainly, what the 0.1.0 package actually contains, and an honest list of the parts that are not finished.

## Help

- [Help](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/help/): Four pages for when something breaks, when a word makes no sense, or when you need to know what is actually switched on before you spend anything.
- [Troubleshooting and common errors](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/help/troubleshooting/): What the message on your screen means, why it happened, and the next thing to do, arranged by what you see rather than by which part of the code complained.
- [Questions worth asking](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/help/faq/): Short honest answers to what people actually ask about ChainBloom, including the several where the answer is no, and the ones where it is not yet.
- [Complete glossary](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/help/glossary/): Every word this documentation uses, defined once in full, in alphabetical order, with links to the pages where each one actually matters.
- [What is running today](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/chainbloom/docs/help/status/): What is live today, what remains unsupported, and how the production ChainBloom read path is verified.
